topics.title: Fractals in nature, the Sierpinski Carpet and fractals in art

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a fractal is a self-similar shape showing the same pattern at smaller and smaller scales, in nature and in art.
Find the number of remaining squares, holes and the remaining area at any step of the Sierpinski Carpet.
Describe the construction of the Sierpinski Triangle and count its triangles, holes and remaining area.
Find the number of sides and the perimeter at the nth step of the Koch Snowflake.
Mentally cut and rearrange simple plane shapes without drawing them.
Identify solids that have given profiles from different viewpoints.

topics.title: Faces, edges and vertices; prisms, pyramids and nets

concepts.learning_objective: Count the faces, edges and vertices of prisms and pyramids, including n-sided ones.
Recognise and reason about nets of cubes, tetrahedrons, cylinders, cones and other solids.
Find the shortest path between two points on the surface of a cuboid by drawing a suitable net and using the Baudhayana Theorem.
Define the projection of a point on a plane and compare the length of a line with its projection.
Identify the front, top and side views of a solid as projections on the vertical, horizontal and side planes.
Relate shadows in sunlight to projections and use the fact that parallel lines project to parallel lines.

topics.title: Isometric projections and drawing on isometric grids

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the isometric projection of a cube and why its edges project to equal lengths.
Draw solids made of cubes on an isometric grid using the length, depth and height axes.
